name: Retention and replay.
line: Topics keep their records, so a reader can go back and read them again.
text: A topic keeps its records under a retention policy: the last n, a time window, or the latest record per key. Where a restarted reader starts is its own choice: `earliest` reads every retained record again, `committed` reads on after its last commit, `latest` takes only new records. A consumer group, whose members share a topic’s records between them, is the exception: once it has committed, it resumes after its commit whatever `from` says. D subscribes from `earliest`, which is how it rebuilds its list of notes.

proof.test: a group resumes from its committed offset whatever `from` says
a crashed D replays its log and shows the same history, with no new events
